MAJOR: TLS classification is now split by error form: typed x509 errors → `tls_error`, but plain-string `x509:` errors → `db_unavailable` via `dbUnavailableMarkers`. Same root cause yields two reasons, so alert rules keyed on `db_unavailable` will fire on TLS misconfig only through the untyped path, partially defeating the new `tls_error` distinction (AC-1 consistency).
MINOR: `"x509:"` is a loose substring marker matched anywhere in the message; unrelated text containing that token (driver/proxy wrappers, SQL fragments) is silently classified `db_unavailable`. Prefer prefix/anchored matching or typed-only classification.

Moving the statement-timeout string check after the typed x509 branch changes precedence with no test pinning it; add a case where text matches both a 57014/statement-timeout and a marker to lock ordering.
No test wraps a typed x509 error (`fmt.Errorf("...: %w", x509.UnknownAuthorityError{})`) to prove `errors.As` traversal still yields `tls_error` through the new branch order.
NIT: Mixing the `tls_error` concept with a `"x509:"` entry inside `dbUnavailableMarkers` obscures intent; a short comment or grouped marker set would make the boundary explicit.
SUMMARY: Delta is small, Go-only, and resolves the prior review findings (typed x509 coverage, fallback boundary, `tls_error` bucket); no blockers.
Top risk: inconsistent TLS reason classification between typed and stringified errors, which can misroute alerts and inflate/deflate the `tls_error` series unexpectedly.
Minor gaps: brittle substring marker and un-pinned classification precedence/wrapping behaviour.
